c1.note: Auto Finance News (Nov 9) and Automotive News (Nov 10) report GM Financial cut 400 jobs 'to support operating performance'.

c2.note: Image caption states net income of $487 million in Q3, down 17% from a year earlier; it is context, not an answer.

c3.note: CNBC and Bloomberg report about 500-600 employees affected starting May 11, 2026; the May date is older than 90 days.

c4.note: Salaried IT employees, largely in Austin, Texas, and Warren, Michigan, per CNBC.

c5.note: CNBC says 'GM confirmed the cuts'; TechCrunch says GM confirmed it conducted layoffs.

c6.note: CNBC: GM confirmed the cuts 'but declined to give specific details about the actions'.

c7.note: The 500-600 figure is attributed to a person familiar with the plans, not to GM.

c8.note: GM's emailed statement: 'GM is transforming its Information Technology organization to better position the company for the future.'

c9.note: GM statement: 'we have made the difficult decision to eliminate certain roles globally.'

c10.note: TechCrunch's source says GM is still hiring IT staff for AI-native development, data engineering, cloud and model-development skills; CNBC also notes 82 open IT roles.

c11.note: The claim is supported, but the statement came from a person familiar with the layoffs rather than GM itself, so the attribution 'GM said' is loose.

c12.note: MLive reported 361 layoffs on Aug 14, 2026; other outlets say 350 from the same WARN notice.

c13.note: MLive says the mass layoff takes effect Jan. 17, 2027, which conflicts with the Jan. 14 date in other outlets.

c14.note: CBS Detroit, WILX and WARN tracker report 350 workers; MLive's 361 differs slightly.

c15.note: CBS, WILX and the WARN tracker give Jan. 14, 2027; MLive's Jan. 17 is the outlier.

c16.note: CBS, WILX and MLive all name the Lansing Grand River Assembly/Stamping and Lansing Regional Stamping sites; January 2027 retooling downtime is also supported (variant F).

c17.note: CBS says the WARN notice was filed Aug. 12 with the Michigan DLEO, and WarnTracker lists a 2026-08-12 notice date for 350 workers.

c18.note: GM's statement ties the cuts to the $1.25B investment and the retooling downtime.

c19.note: GM statement: 'We anticipate recalling affected employees back to Lansing Grand River at the end of the retooling period.'

c20.note: MLive, citing the Detroit News, says the facilities will be retooled for future production including the Cadillac CT5.

c21.note: A GM spokesperson said the skilled-trades team will prepare the plant for next-gen CT5 production.

c22.note: GM spokesperson Kevin Kelly said impacted employees may be eligible for SUB pay equal to 74% of hourly wage under the GM-UAW contract.

c23.note: Unifor release dated Jan. 29, 2026 says the final third shift is Jan. 30, with more than 700 direct jobs cut and hundreds more at suppliers.

c24.note: The Unifor release says GM reported more than $12 billion that week; the snippet is cut off, but it fits GM's 2025 results, so confidence is medium.

c25.note: The article reports about 200 layoffs at Ramos Arizpe tied to the end of ICE Blazer production in October 2026.

c26.note: WarnTracker lists 1,334 affected at Ultium Cells in Warren/Trumbull, Ohio, effective 2026-01-05; variant C's 'unconfirmed' wording is overly hedged but the figure is supported.

c27.note: WarnTracker shows 710 at the Ultium Cells facility in Maury County, TN, with layoff date 2026-01-05.

c28.note: Reuters, March 30, 2026: Factory ZERO idled until April 13, temporarily laying off 1,300 workers.

c29.note: Direct quote from a GM spokesperson in Reuters.

c30.note: WSWS says about 1,145 positions were eliminated at Factory Zero and WarnTracker lists 1,140, consistent with about 1,100 cuts; this is a secondary source, so confidence is medium.

c31.note: WSWS (dated Oct 21, 2026) says Brownstown closure was confirmed Tuesday, closing when lease expires summer 2027; Oct 21, 2026 is a Wednesday per calendar? Oct 20 is Tuesday, so the exact day is slightly uncertain, but the article is dated 21 Oct.

c32.note: Passage states about 300 once employed, fewer than a dozen remain, and GM offers remaining workers other placements.

c33.note: Passage says GM announced the $20B buyback the same day the Brownstown closure was confirmed.

c3.note: CNBC (May 11, 2026): global cuts began Monday and affect about 500–600 employees, mostly in Austin and Warren.

c7.note: CNBC credits the figure to a person familiar with the plans who was not authorized to speak publicly, not to GM.

c13.note: MLive says the mass layoff takes effect Jan. 17, 2027. WILX and other outlets give Jan. 14, 2027, but the claim is only about what MLive reported.

c16.note: CBS Detroit, WILX and MLive all name Lansing Grand River Assembly/Stamping and Lansing Regional Stamping.

c19.note: GM statement: 'We anticipate recalling affected employees back to Lansing Grand River at the end of the retooling period.'

c21.note: WILX (Aug 17, 2026) quotes a GM spokesperson saying the skilled-trades team will prepare the plant for the next-generation Cadillac CT5.
